source.lineage: Late-1960s through 1970s British Invasion-derived guitar-pop subgenre codified through the Who (the term power pop was coined by Pete Townshend to describe the Whos sound), Big Star (the Memphis power-pop band, #1 Record 1972, Radio City 1974), Badfinger (the Apple Records 1970-72 power-pop voice), Cheap Trick (the mainstream-commercial post-Big-Star extension), the Raspberries, the Knack (My Sharona 1979 the commercial breakthrough); foundational sound: melodic-hook-centric three-minute songs with chord-driven electric guitars, harmony vocals, and tight rhythm-section foundation

extras.description: Power pop (codified 1972 onward through Big Star and Badfinger establishing the sound, with second-wave 1979-1981 commercial-mainstream era through Cheap Trick, The Knack, and the Cars, and continuing tradition through to present), the hooky guitar-pop subgenre. Defined by hooky melodic-foreground songwriting with tight verse-pre-chorus-chorus pop-craft architecture, full-throated vocal harmonies stacking 2-4 voices in arranged harmony parts, ringing distortion-touched guitars (the power-pop-specific guitar-tone of clean Rickenbacker or Telecaster pushed slightly into amp-overdrive), hard backbeat percussion with prominent fills, song-content addressing teenage-romantic-and-relationship subjects, and tight 3-3:30 song-length. Production lineage descends from late-Beatles-era and Who-and-Move British-Invasion power-pop precursors. Distinguished from straight pop by retention of band-instrumentation foreground over orchestrated arrangement; distinguished from punk by full-vocal-harmony and clean-guitar aesthetic; distinguished from later jangle pop by retention of hard-rock distortion-tinge.

extras.description: Swamp rock emerged in the late 1960s as bands imagined a Louisiana bayou idiom through blues, rockabilly and swamp pop — most influentially Creedence Clearwater Revival, who were from El Cerrito, California, and cut the records at Wally Heider's San Francisco studio. The sound is deliberately lean: two guitars with tremolo and spring reverb, no solos longer than they need to be, an unhurried backbeat, and hoarse Southern-inflected vocals telling short cautionary stories. It is sparser and more riff-based than Allman-style Southern rock, and rooted in Gulf Coast blues rather than the country-and-jam vocabulary of that scene.

extras.description: New Romanticism began as a London club-dress movement in 1979 and became, within three years, the dominant sound of British chart pop and early MTV. source.name: Roots Rock

extras.description: Roots rock is the late-1960s turn away from studio psychedelia toward older American forms, announced by The Band's Music from Big Pink and Dylan's John Wesley Harding and carried commercially by Creedence Clearwater Revival. Its markers are dry unprocessed guitar and drums, prominent acoustic piano and Hammond, rotating lead vocals with rough gospel-style harmony, and songwriting drawn from country, hymnody, blues and rockabilly rather than blues-rock virtuosity. It differs from country rock by leaning on rhythm-and-blues and gospel as much as on Nashville, and from the Americana that later descends from it by belonging to a mainstream rock market rather than an alt-country one.

source.name: Cambodian Rock (Phnom Penh Psych)
source.lineage: Phnom Penh popular music of roughly 1963-1975, made by Sinn Sisamouth, Ros Serey Sothea, Pen Ran and Yol Aularong for radio and nightclub, grafting surf-reverb and fuzz guitar, combo organ, Farfisa-and-saxophone bandstand arrangements and a-go-go or slow-rock backbeats onto Khmer ramvong and romvong dance rhythms, with high, nasal, heavily ornamented Khmer vocal delivery on top.

extras.description: Cambodian rock formed when American Forces radio and French yé-yé records reached Phnom Penh nightclubs, and it kept Khmer melodic ornament and vocal placement intact while borrowing wholesale from surf, garage and soul instrumentation. Recordings are dry-to-slapback, often small-room and lightly overdubbed, with organ and reverbed guitar sharing the top and horns arranged in unison stabs. What separates it from Thai string and Vietnamese kích động nhạc of the same years is the vocal line: intensely melismatic, high-set, and phrased against the beat rather than with it. The scene ended abruptly in 1975, and most of its principals were killed.

source.name: Deathrock
source.lineage: Los Angeles offshoot of punk formed 1979-1983 around Christian Death, 45 Grave, Kommunity FK and Super Heroines — mid-tempo 100-140 BPM tom-heavy tribal drumming, high melodic bass carrying the riff, thin chorused and heavily reverbed guitar playing single-note minor figures, cheap string synth or organ pads and declamatory, theatrical vocals over horror and decadence imagery.

extras.description: Deathrock is the American, punk-descended branch of gothic rock, born in Los Angeles clubs like the Vex and the Cathay de Grande around 1980. The rhythm section inverts rock convention — bass takes the melodic lead while guitar supplies scraping chorus-and-delay atmospherics and the drums lean on floor toms and open snare rather than backbeat — and the vocals are spoken, shouted and wailed rather than sung. It is rawer, faster and more punk-rooted than English goth rock, and unlike horror punk it stays in minor tonality and plays the horror straight.
